title: Panda tree
description: A tree diagram of chains and branches. A chain is an ordered list of points; any point can grow branches (each another chain); a leaf ends its chain. Rules a schema can't express (a leaf must be the last point of its chain) are checked by `bun run check`. Guide: docs/reference/json-format.md

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, for editor support.

format.description: Written by panda on export; optional.

version.description: Written by panda on export; optional.

direction.description: Flow of the main chain: LR left → right, TB top → bottom, RL, BT.

edgeStyle.description: sides: lines attach to fixed sides of the points. shortest: straight lines between the nearest borders.

layout.description: stacked: every branch gets its own rows. packed: compact, good for many leaves per point.

chain.description: Points in order: each one follows the previous. Only the last point may be a leaf.

id.description: Stable id; generated when missing. Keep ids when editing a saved tree.

kind.description: leaf: ends its chain; must be the last point of its chain and has no branches.

content.description: Plain text under the title; use \n for new lines.

pin.description: Position set by dragging in the editor, in layout grid units. Usually left out.

collapsed.description: Branches hidden in the editor. Omit when false.

branches.description: Each branch is a chain (an array of points) starting beside this point. A side ending is a branch holding one leaf: [[{"kind": "leaf", "title": "Done"}]].
